summary: We implement programmable energy-selective local reservoirs in superconducting qubits by parametrically modulating coupling to readout resonators, achieving incoherent pump and loss that autonomously stabilize entangled Bell states. We demonstrate stabilization of the single-excitation state $|{-}\rangle$ with $90.8\%$ fidelity using a two-qubit transmon array with $J \approx 2\pi \times 6$ MHz and validate characterization via robust classical shadow estimation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a scalable approach to stabilizing correlated many-body states in superconducting circuits, but existing implementations require dedicated hardware or coherent drives that limit scalability and flexibility in qubit arrays.
method: We use parametric sideband coupling between transmons and their readout resonators (via flux-modulation waveforms at red and blue sidebands) to create energy-selective local dissipation with bandwidth $\kappa_r \approx 2\pi \times 1.5$ MHz, enabling incoherent pump ($g_S = 2\pi \times 0.75$ MHz) and loss ($g_D = 2\pi \times 0.58$ MHz) on individual qubits without additional hardware.
result: Starting from $|gg\rangle$, we reach steady-state fidelity $F = 90.8\%$ to $|{-}\rangle$ within $2$ μs with concurrence $C \approx 0.82$; dominant infidelity sources are resonator thermal population ($2.5\%$, contributing $5.5\%$ error), intrinsic relaxation ($T_1^{|{-}\rangle} = 50$ μs, $2.4\%$ error), and off-resonant transitions ($1.6\%$ error), all mitigable via existing techniques.
